proposals.after: The king asked: 'How do you know it?'
proposals.reason: Literal English omits required grammar and obscures 王問：「何以知之？」.

proposals.before: With this know it, thus wished go.'
proposals.after: With this I knew it, and so I wished to go.'
proposals.reason: Literal English drops subject and verbs needed to render 以此知之，故欲往.

proposals.before: Xiangru judged that the king of Qin was feigning and pretended to offer Zhao cities, but in truth could not obtain them, and said to the king of Qin: "The He Shi bi is a treasure transmitted throughout the world. The king of Zhao was afraid and did not dare not present it.
proposals.after: Xiangru judged that the king of Qin was only feigning an offer of cities to Zhao, which in truth could not be obtained, and said to the king of Qin: "The He Shi bi is a treasure transmitted throughout the world. The king of Zhao was afraid and did not dare not present it.
proposals.reason: Literal 'feigning and pretended' is redundant, and 'could not obtain them' misreads 實不可得 as Qin's failure to obtain rather than the cities' unavailability to Zhao.

proposals.before: Lin Xiangru stepped forward and said: 'The Zhao king hears that the Qin king is skilled in Qin music. Please strike the chime stones for the Qin king to provide mutual entertainment.'
proposals.after: Lin Xiangru stepped forward and said: 'The Zhao king hears that the Qin king is skilled in Qin music. Please play the fou, King of Qin, so we may entertain one another.'
proposals.reason: Chinese 請奏盆缻秦王 asks the Qin king himself to strike the fou; the idiomatic rendering reverses the agent as if someone else strikes for him.

proposals.before: Lin Xiangru went forward said: 'Zhao king secretly heard Qin king skilled at Qin music, please strike basin for Qin king, to mutually entertain.'
proposals.after: Lin Xiangru went forward said: 'Zhao king secretly heard Qin king skilled at Qin music; please, Qin king, strike the basin, to mutually entertain.'
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise makes the Qin king the beneficiary rather than the performer of 奏盆缻秦王.

proposals.before: Qin king sent envoy inform Zhao king, wished with king make friendly meeting at west river outside Mianchi pool.
proposals.after: The Qin king sent an envoy to inform the Zhao king that he wished to hold a friendly meeting with the king at Mianchi outside the west river.
proposals.reason: Literal English is missing articles and finite verbs so badly that the diplomatic invitation is hard to parse.

proposals.before: Thus, Xiangru forward advanced chime stones, thus knelt requested Qin king.
proposals.after: Thus Xiangru advanced the chime stones forward and knelt to request the Qin king.
proposals.reason: Word order and missing function words obscure that Xiangru presents the fou and kneels in request.

proposals.before: The next year Zhao She defeated the Qin army at Yuyu.
proposals.after: The next year Zhao She defeated the Qin army at Eyu.
proposals.reason: Literal renders 閼與 as Yuyu while the idiomatic correctly uses Eyu; standardize the place name.

proposals.before: Qin attacked Han, army at Yan.
proposals.after: Qin attacked Han, army at Eyu.
proposals.reason: Literal mistranslates 閼與 as Yan; the place is Eyu (same as elsewhere in the chapter).

proposals.before: Spy reported to Qin general, Qin general greatly delighted said: 'Having left capital thirty li yet army not advance, moreover increases fortifications, Yan is not Zhao territory.'
proposals.after: Spy reported to Qin general, Qin general greatly delighted said: 'Having left capital thirty li yet army not advance, moreover increases fortifications, Eyu is not Zhao territory.'
proposals.reason: Literal again renders 閼與 as Yan instead of Eyu.

proposals.before: Zhao She having sent away Qin spy, rolled up armor and hurried to it, two days one night arrived, ordered good archers to go fifty li from Yan and camp.
proposals.after: Zhao She having sent away Qin spy, rolled up armor and hurried to it, two days one night arrived, ordered good archers to go fifty li from Eyu and camp.
proposals.reason: Literal renders 閼與 as Yan; should be Eyu.

proposals.before: Zhao She said: "Wait until after the battle; then we will settle it at Handan."
proposals.after: Zhao She said: "Wait for a later order at Handan."
proposals.reason: Idiomatic invents 'after the battle'; Chinese 胥後令邯鄲 means wait for a subsequent order (to be settled) at Handan.

proposals.before: In the seventh year, Qin and Zhao confronted each other at Changping. Zhao She was already dead, and Lin Xiangru was gravely ill. Zhao put Lian Po in command against Qin, but after Qin defeated the Zhao army several times, Lian Po fortified his camp and refused battle.
proposals.after: In the seventh year, Qin and Zhao confronted each other at Changping. Zhao She was already dead, and Lin Xiangru was gravely ill. Zhao put Lian Po in command against Qin; Qin defeated the Zhao army several times, and the Zhao army fortified its walls and would not fight.
proposals.reason: Chinese 趙軍固壁不戰 makes the Zhao army the subject that held the walls; the idiomatic version wrongly attributes fortifying the camp to Lian Po personally.

proposals.before: She replied, "When I first served his father as general, he personally brought food and drink to feed dozens of men, befriended hundreds, and gave all the king's and royal family's rewards to army officers and gentlemen. On the day he received orders, he never asked about family matters.
proposals.after: She replied, "When I first served his father, at the time he was general, he personally brought food and drink to feed dozens of men, befriended hundreds, and gave all the great king's and royal clan's rewards to army officers and gentlemen. On the day he received orders, he never asked about family matters.
proposals.reason: Chinese 始妾事其父，時為將 means she served his father when he was general; 'as general' must not modify her service.

proposals.before: Kuo army defeated, several tens of thousands crowd thus surrendered Qin, Qin all buried them alive.
proposals.after: Kuo army defeated, a crowd of several hundred thousand thus surrendered to Qin, Qin buried them all alive.
proposals.reason: 數十萬 means several hundred thousand, not several tens of thousands (數萬).

proposals.before: He appointed officials as needed and had all market rents enter the commander's residence to fund the soldiers' expenses.
proposals.after: He appointed officials as needed and had all market rents enter the headquarters to fund the soldiers' expenses.
proposals.reason: 莫府 is 幕府, the military headquarters/command tent, not a personal residence.

proposals.before: Used expediency placed officials, market rents all entered Mo residence, for soldiers expenses.
proposals.after: Used expediency placed officials, market rents all entered headquarters, for soldiers expenses.
proposals.reason: 莫府 should be rendered as headquarters (mofu), not the transliteration Mo residence.

proposals.before: Zhao Wang Qian seventh year, Qin sent Wang Jian attacked Zhao, Zhao sent Li Mu, Sima Shang defended against them.
proposals.after: Zhao Wang Qian seventh year, Qin sent Wang Jian to attack Zhao; Zhao sent Li Mu and Sima Shang to defend against them.
proposals.reason: Literal English omits the infinitive marker after 'sent' and runs two clauses together, obscuring that Qin dispatched Wang Jian to attack and Zhao separately dispatched the defenders.

decisions.reason: 王問：「何以知之？」 is already clear in the telegraphic literal “King asked: 'How know it?'”; adding articles and “do you” only polishes literal register toward idiomatic style without correcting a semantic error.
以此知之，故欲往 is adequately rendered by the telegraphic literal; inserting “I knew” and “wished to go” is stylistic smoothing of the literal field, not a fix of mistranslated sense.

特以詐詳為予趙城，實不可得 means Qin only pretended to give Zhao cities that could not actually be obtained; “could not obtain them” wrongly implies Qin’s inability, and the proposed literal restores the cities as unobtainable.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 特以詐詳為予趙城，實不可得

decisions.reason: 請奏盆缻秦王 asks the Qin king himself to play the fou; confirmed by 秦王不肯擊缻. The original “strike … for the Qin king” reverses the agent, and “fou” correctly replaces “chime stones.”

sourceWitness.excerpt: 請奏盆缻秦王，以相娛樂

decisions.reason: 奏盆缻秦王 makes the Qin king the performer, not the beneficiary; “strike basin for Qin king” reverses agent/patient, and the proposed literal restores vocative request that he strike the basin.

會於西河外澠池 places the meeting at Mianchi outside the West River; the original “west river outside Mianchi pool” inverts that geography, and the proposed literal restores the correct place order while clarifying the invitation.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 欲與王為好會於西河外澠池

decisions.reason: 前進缻，因跪請秦王 is already recoverable from the telegraphic literal; reordering words without fixing the wrong “chime stones” for 缻 is merely stylistic polish of the literal field.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 於是相如前進缻，因跪請秦王

decisions.reason: 閼與 is the place Eyu, already used correctly in the idiomatic and related claims; “Yuyu” is a wrong reading of the same toponym and should be standardized to Eyu.
軍於閼與 is Eyu, not Yan (燕); the literal’s “Yan” is a place-name error, and Eyu matches the chapter’s other renderings of 閼與.
閼與非趙地也 again names Eyu; rendering it as “Yan” invents a different polity/place and must be corrected to Eyu.
去閼與五十里而軍 refers to distance from Eyu; “Yan” is the same 閼與 mistranslation and the proposed Eyu is correct.
胥後令邯鄲 means wait for a later order at Handan; “after the battle” is invented content absent from the Chinese, and the proposed idiomatic removes that addition.
秦數敗趙軍，趙軍固壁不戰 makes 趙軍 the subject that held the walls; attributing fortifying the camp to Lian Po personally misstates the Chinese subject.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 秦數敗趙軍，趙軍固壁不戰

decisions.reason: 始妾事其父，時為將 means she served his father when he was general; “served his father as general” wrongly attaches 為將 to her service, and the proposed wording restores the correct attachment plus 大王及宗室.
數十萬之眾 is several hundred thousand, not several tens of thousands (數萬); the proposed literal restores the correct numeral scale.
莫府 is 幕府, the military headquarters, not a personal “commander’s residence”; the proposed idiomatic matches that institutional sense.
莫府 should be headquarters (幕府), not the transliteration “Mo residence”; the proposed literal corrects that naming error.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 市租皆輸入莫府，為士卒費

decisions.reason: 秦使王翦攻趙，趙使李牧、司馬尚御之 are two parallel dispatch clauses; the original can be read as if only Sima Shang defended, and the proposed literal restores both Li Mu and Sima Shang as defenders sent by Zhao.
